problem_statement: The RISC-V PMP (Physical Memory Protection) subsystem needs a way to reset its configuration. A caller requires a function that clears and disables every unlocked PMP entry, returning each to a disabled (Null Region / OFF) state, while leaving any entry that is locked completely unchanged. Before performing the change it must establish a predictable machine-mode privilege context (MPRV cleared so accesses use M-mode privilege, and MPP set to M-mode). After the call, the M-Status state must reflect MPRV disabled and MPP set to M-mode. A caller reads back the PMP configuration registers to verify the result.

verification.reason: The statement omits several public interface and configuration details required by the hidden checks, but all missing pieces can be added as interface/behaviour requirements without dictating the implementation.

problems.detail: The hidden test calls z_riscv_pmp_clear_all and includes zephyr/arch/riscv/pmp.h, but the statement does not give the function name, the header path, or the fact that the header must make the function available to callers.
The hidden test calls z_riscv_pmp_read_config(unsigned long *, size_t), but the statement only says a caller reads back the PMP configuration and does not give the required name or signature.
The hidden test expects each unlocked pmpcfg byte to be exactly 0x00, while the statement only says the entry is disabled or OFF.
The hidden test checks the pre-call M-Status state (MPRV enabled and MPP not M-mode), which the statement does not specify as the expected calling context.
The test depends on CONFIG_RISCV_PMP being enabled and on CONFIG_ZTEST being enabled so the read-back helper is externally linked, but the statement does not mention these configuration dependencies.

problem_statement_fixed: The RISC-V PMP (Physical Memory Protection) subsystem needs a way to reset its configuration. A caller requires a function named z_riscv_pmp_clear_all(void), declared in include/zephyr/arch/riscv/pmp.h and available when CONFIG_RISCV_PMP is enabled, that clears and disables every unlocked PMP entry, returning each unlocked pmpcfg byte to 0x00 (disabled Null Region / OFF), while leaving any entry that is locked (PMP_L set) completely unchanged. The expected calling context is that MPRV is enabled and MPP is not M-mode before the call. Before performing the change it must establish a predictable machine-mode privilege context (MPRV cleared so accesses use M-mode privilege, and MPP set to M-mode). After the call, the M-Status state must reflect MPRV disabled and MPP set to M-mode. A caller reads back the PMP configuration registers to verify the result using z_riscv_pmp_read_config(unsigned long *pmp_cfg, size_t pmp_cfg_size), which stores pmpcfg CSR contents into pmp_cfg for pmp_cfg_size unsigned long entries and must have external linkage when CONFIG_ZTEST is enabled so external callers can capture the configuration before and after the call.
